headline: High: TREK’s collaborative, MCP-enabled defaults can ingest and act on ComfyUI outputs, creating prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error risks; ComfyUI itself is offline but the pair interaction is unsafe.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI can expose file-based workflows and outputs, while TREK explicitly uses MCP and a real-time collaborative model. That creates a plausible bridge where TREK ingests ComfyUI-generated content as instructions or data. ComfyUI is offline by default, so this is not a direct remote injection path, but the shared content channel is enough for medium risk.
conditions: IF TREK ingests ComfyUI-generated files or messages as trusted instructions
IF a shared MCP or workspace channel is configured between the agents
mitigations: Disable automatic parsing of ComfyUI outputs in TREK
Require provenance tags on all imported workflow files
Route ComfyUI outputs through a human review step
Restrict MCP tools to read-only for the shared channel
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-separation guards

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches model assets and local files, while TREK handles reservations, documents, API keys, and MFA secrets and can use MCP plus allowlisted network egress. If the pair shares a workspace or TREK imports ComfyUI artifacts, sensitive travel data can leak into outputs or logs. The interaction is plausible in default self-hosted setups, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or upload directory
IF TREK logs or forwards imported artifacts containing secrets or reservations
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct storage volumes
Exclude secrets and reservation files from TREK uploads
Turn off verbose logging for imported artifacts
Review MCP permissions before enabling shared access
requires-engineering: implement per-data-class redaction before export

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI has no filesystem write, subprocess, or git modification capability, while TREK supports collaborative sessions and multiple instances. There is little direct write-write overlap, so conflict is limited. The main concern is coordination on shared mutable resources if TREK is pointed at the same workspace, which is an unusual configuration.
conditions: IF TREK and ComfyUI are configured to mutate the same shared directory
IF multiple TREK sessions edit the same travel database concurrently
mitigations: Keep ComfyUI and TREK on separate directories
Avoid concurrent edits to shared files
Use file locks for any shared workspace
Limit TREK to one active writer per dataset
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in, so it may treat upstream content as actionable. ComfyUI can generate workflows, images, or metadata that TREK could render or use without verification. That creates a plausible chain where a bad ComfyUI output propagates into travel plans or reservations, but the evidence does not show direct automation, so medium fits.
conditions: IF TREK consumes ComfyUI outputs without validation
IF generated content is used to populate travel plans, reservations, or messages
mitigations: Add a verification step before TREK acts on imported content
Mark ComfyUI outputs as untrusted by default
Require human approval for reservation-affecting actions
Log source provenance for every imported artifact
requires-engineering: separate generation from execution in the workflow

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles reservations, documents, country visit history, email addresses, API keys, and MFA secrets, while ComfyUI is an image-generation tool with local model assets and offline operation. If travel data or identity documents are routed through ComfyUI workflows, retention and residency expectations can diverge. The profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF EU PII or travel documents are processed through ComfyUI workflows
IF TREK retention or logging policies differ from the handling applied to imported artifacts
mitigations: Keep travel documents out of ComfyUI workflows
Minimize retention of imported artifacts in TREK logs
Review data-class handling before enabling shared pipelines
Restrict access to secrets and MFA material
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries per data class
